title: Development of a hybrid artificial intelligence framework for pharmacotherapy optimization

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Development of a hybrid artificial intelligence framework for pharmacotherapy optimization》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Aim · Par12】The aim of this study was to develop a relevance-driven, clinician-supervised hybrid AI framework for pharmacotherapy optimization. In this framework, hybrid AI combines retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), deterministic safety rules, and LLM-based reasoning. Specifically, the study sought to derive design principles and translate them into a conceptual architecture designed to support, rather than replace, clinical reasoning in pharmacotherapy optimization.

【Introduction · Par11】Pharmacotherapy optimization in multimorbid patients is increasingly complex due to polypharmacy, expanding electronic health records (EHR), drug shortages, and workforce constraints, resulting in the need to make individualized decisions under time pressure [1–4]. Conventional clinical decision support systems (CDSS) remain largely rule-based and frequently generate alerts rather than context-sensitive reasoning, contributing to limited clinical impact and alert fatigue [5–11]. Pharmacotherapy optimization has evolved toward individualized, goal-oriented care that integrates patient preferences, clinical context, and interprofessional decision-making [12]. As complexity increases, approaches that structure and prioritize clinically relevant information may offer an alternative to traditional static rule-based decision support [13–15]. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers the potential to support this transition by enabling automated data integration and contextual interpretation. While specific models for pharmacotherapy optimization are scarce, AI is widely accepted among healthcare professionals [16–18]. The recently developed MedinAI guidelines highlight the need for transparent reporting of AI applications in medicines and pharmacotherapy, including model architecture, data sources, human oversight, and ethical considerations [19]. However, stand-alone models, particularly large language models (LLMs), remain unreliable in complex pharmacotherapy without structured clinical context and transparent justification [20–23]. Safe and clinically meaningful decision support therefore may require integration of AI with established safety mechanisms, longitudinal patient data, and clinician oversight.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Development of a hybrid artificial intelligence framework for pharmacotherapy optimization》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Design principles · Par18】Pharmacotherapy optimization consists of distinct clinical activities with different risk profiles, information requirements, and frequencies [12, 15, 26]. Decomposition may facilitate meaningful digital support and avoid indiscriminate automation of complex clinical decision-making [26]. For example, a comprehensive medication review can be decomposed into distinct tasks such as acquiring data, performing the patient assessment, setting therapeutic goals, assessing medication safety or evaluation of guideline adherence. Such decomposition enables targeted digital support while preserving clinician oversight of the overall decision-making process.

【Design principles · Par20】CDSS should prioritize information according to clinical relevance, patient vulnerability, and context-specific actionability. Within this framework, AI structures clinical relevance by identifying issues that most urgently require professional judgement rather than replacing decision-making. For example, a clinically significant drug-related problem associated with serious harm would be prioritized over minor informational alerts, allowing decision support to focus attention on issues most relevant to patient outcomes and therapeutic decision-making [20].

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Development of a hybrid artificial intelligence framework for pharmacotherapy optimization》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · Par47】This study resulted in a relevance-driven, clinician-supervised hybrid AI framework for pharmacotherapy optimization that integrates hybrid reasoning, patient-specific context, and clinician governance. Therapeutic complexity, expanding electronic health records, workforce strain, and rising expectations for clinical contribution have challenged traditional approaches to pharmacotherapy optimization. Manual optimization may become increasingly difficult to scale in response to growing therapeutic complexity, expanding clinical data, and workforce constraints. This framework outlines a conceptual blueprint for a clinician-supervised, multimodal hybrid AI framework embedded in a digital closed loop with the patient, designed to augment, rather than replace, professional judgement. A central feature of the framework is the integration of patient-specific clinical data, longitudinal information, and patient preferences to support individualized pharmacotherapy optimization. The proposed framework provides a conceptual foundation to guide future research, implementation, and evaluation of AI-supported pharmacotherapy optimization systems.

【Results · abstract-4-1】Seven design principles were identified, including decomposition of clinical activities, relevance-based prioritization, hybrid reasoning under clinician oversight, integration of patient goals, transparency of evidence sources, longitudinal optimization within a governed closed loop, and evaluation as a design requirement. These principles informed a conceptual architecture integrating structured clinical data, patient preferences, longitudinal patient information, and evidence retrieval within a clinician-governed decision-support framework.
